summary: Your CI list stays stable and complete, and you now see every user's sign-in methods.

new.title: See every user's sign-in methods
new.text: SecurityInsight now reads each user's sign-in methods in full, including the device a key lives on. A setting chooses every user, privileged users only or none.

new.title: Assumptions page shows collection scope in force
new.text: The Assumptions page shows every collection-scope setting with the value in force.

new.title: Close-loop table names every finding
new.text: An asset's close-loop table names each finding with its title and kind, such as CVE, recommendation or certificate, and counts every item.

fixes.title: One stable CI per machine
fixes.text: A merged CI's id is never reused, and a CI that returned after a merge is retired into the right CI with its findings. Nothing is deleted.

fixes.title: ServiceNow learns every CI state and reason
fixes.text: Every inactive CI is sent to ServiceNow with its state and a plain reason, such as merged or not seen since a date. No CI is ever dropped.

fixes.title: Gone machines retire after their grace period
fixes.text: A device or Azure resource that only Microsoft's security data still lists now retires after its grace period. Dormant accounts stay, as a risk to report.

fixes.title: Private installs cost nothing between updates
fixes.text: The machines that prepare a private installation's updates run only while they work and scale to none afterwards. Upkeep of large tables pauses whenever an update waits.

fixes.title: Smaller fixes
fixes.text: An Azure VM's SQL Server is linked under the VM's CI, and nameless Defender devices get a generated name. Every CI is rebuilt once after this update.
